frontier.hypothesis: The last 11 blend insns fall if the three channel sums are LOCAL quantities that local-alloc seats on $v0 before global_alloc runs - which requires breaking local-alloc's combine_regs merge of the red sum into r_src's quantity (pseudo 123, $a1) without creating a new global allocno.
frontier.mechanism: local_alloc runs before global_alloc; a pseudo it assigns is hard-numbered, so global_conflicts records it as a HARD-REG conflict for overlapping allocnos. A red sum locally seated on $v0 therefore puts regno 2 into the blue temp's conflict set, which is the only measured-cheap way to get regno 2 into pass0_used and make find_reg return 4 ($a0). Today combine_regs ties the sum's quantity to r_src's because r_src dies in the add, and the merged quantity spans blocks and becomes global allocno 123.
frontier.next_probe: Read tmp/grind/func_8003DE14/dumps/*.lreg for the blend block (pwsh tools/grinder/dump.ps1 func_8003DE14 on the d2 body) and identify the quantity numbers for the red sum and r_src; then sweep source shapes that keep r_src live past the add (so combine_regs cannot merge) WITHOUT adding a reference that combine cannot fold - e.g. deriving r_ch from r_src rather than from the sum, or ordering the arm so the red sum's def and r_src's last use are separated by the green channel's mult. Accept only forms with build_insns 173 whose BB2_FINDREG_DEBUG=<blue temp> prints 2 inside conflicts and whose alloc row for px still prints hardreg=4.

frontier.hypothesis: The regs_someone_prefers route is reachable: a later-allocated global allocno with a hard-reg preference for $v0 excludes $v0 from the blue temp's pass-0 set without adding a register-pressure shift, because a preference costs nothing in the allocno order that the blue temp sees.
frontier.mechanism: find_reg's pass 0 ORs regs_someone_prefers[allocno] into `used` (global.c:1001), and prune_preferences builds that set from the hard_reg_full_preferences of allocnos LATER in allocno_order that do not conflict. set_preference (global.c:1671) creates such a preference when a reg-reg copy has one hard-numbered side, so a locally-allocated $v0 value copied into a lower-priority named local would do it.
frontier.next_probe: On the d2 body, introduce a named local in the blend arm (or in the latch, which is the same loop body) that is a PLAIN COPY of a value local-alloc has already seated on $v0 - the cheapest candidate is the or-chain accumulator's `pixel & 0x8000` staged into a local that is read once after the blue channel - and dump BB2_FINDREG_DEBUG for the blue temp to see whether regno 2 appears in someone_prefers. Score only forms with build_insns 173.

frontier.hypothesis: An ordinary-C carrier exists for the g_src price (the weaker of the two FAKE extenders): g_src needs any pricing above px's 32727, i.e. nrefs >= 14 at livelen 12, with no upper bound to respect, and the new d2 shape gives g_src a second real consumer it did not have in s21.
frontier.mechanism: pri = floor_log2(nrefs)*nrefs*10000/livelen, and the only thing g_src must beat is px's 32727 so that global.c allocates g_src first and seats it on $v1 while px falls to $a0. In d2 the green sum is already staged through `sum`, so a spelling that reads g_src twice at inner-loop depth 3 (weight +3 each) is one real extra reference away from 35000.
frontier.next_probe: Sweep ordinary-C spellings on the d2 body that give g_src one extra REAL reference at depth 3 - deriving b_src from g_src's pre-shift value, splitting `g_ch = (sum >> 10) & 0x3E0` so g_src is re-read, writing the green product as a compound-assignment chain - and accept only forms with build_insns 173 whose alloc row for pseudo 126 prints pri > 32727 and hardreg=3 with NO chain extender present. c2 (d2 minus the extender) is the 23 baseline to beat.
